claim: Not redundant — but over-built. The finally is the only caret clear for four paths, and in all four closeText() is never reached after the last text frame: (1) stream ends with no terminal frame — read() returns done:true after a text frame (proxy timeout, server shutdown/CancelledError, killed generator); the post-loop code at 554-555 drops the thinking indicator and removes only an *empty* bubble, so the caret survives, and the next turn's reset at 531 nulls curTextEl without touching the class, so it blinks for the rest of the session. (2) reader.read()/api() throws mid-stream: catch at 556-560 removes only an empty bubble. (3) a text frame after a terminal frame in the same response (done's closeText nulls curTextEl; the stray text reopens a bubble and adds .streaming, then the loop exits). (4) any exception escaping handleFrame inside the read loop — structurally (2). Every other frame type (tool_start 456, tool_done 460, ask_user 465/472, done 489, error 495) calls closeText(), which is exactly what commit 1069fce added, so the sweep finds nothing there. The *breadth* of the sweep is yagni: .streaming is added at exactly one site (449), always to curTextEl; curTextEl is nulled only by closeText() (343, which removes the class first) and by the per-turn reset (531), which can only run after the previous turn's finally because send() is gated on !busy (526, 533). (ii) 477's inline '// the caret is stopped by closeText() below' is the same rent paid twice: given 341-343, the next line's closeText() is self-evident; that note exists because the diff deleted a classList.remove from a line the reader never saw. (iii) 562 is the comment that pays — it names why the finally exists — but it is also wrong/incomplete: the sweep's most common cover is a stream that simply *ends* without a terminal frame, no exception and no abort, so 'aborts and exceptions' describes only half its job.
